_comment: Copy to config.json on the Pi and fill in. config.json is gitignored:
it holds the panel password and must never be committed.
bind: the addresses the panel listens on - a list, one listener per
address: the Pi's LAN address (wlan0, what the phone reaches it on)
and its WireGuard address (wg0, 10.77.0.10 in wireguard.md). NOT
0.0.0.0 - the server refuses that, in a list too, because the Pi
joins networks you do not control. An address the box does not
have yet (wg0 comes up late) is retried until it can be bound. A
plain string is still accepted, as older configs have it.
dashboard_url: live.py, on the loopback. The panel is the front door:
the telemetry views and the owner API are reverse-proxied to it
behind the panel's auth, and share links (/s/...) pass straight
through with live.py's own token check. f10-dashboard.service binds
live.py to 127.0.0.1 so this is the only way in.
trusted_proxies: addresses whose X-Forwarded-For/-Proto/-Host are
believed and passed on - the reverse proxy in front of this panel
(the VPS nginx over wg0, once it exists), by its address as this
panel sees it. Empty: the panel is the edge and REPLACES whatever
a client sent with its own values. Never a LAN or phone address.
password: generate one, do not reuse anything. On the Pi:
python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(24))'
Basic auth over plain HTTP puts this on the wire base64-encoded on
every request, so treat it as a LAN-only secret with no other use.
git_remote: the pin. `pull` verifies origin matches this EXACTLY and
refuses otherwise, so the update channel cannot be repointed at
another repository. Copy it from `git -C <repo> remote get-url origin`.
